decisions.rationale: One today, AI->IA, from 2 false positives in 8 real items. An allowlist grown by guessing is a place to hide real failures.

decisions.decision: The entity check is advisory, never blocking
decisions.rationale: These are drafts and a human reads every line; a blocking gate would stop an edition over a token the reviewer was about to fix. What matters is that it is INVOKED.

decisions.decision: capture-published refuses while draft: true (exit 1), and zero matched links is exit 2
decisions.rationale: Recording the model's output as the human's would make every later measurement the model grading itself; and 'the human cut every item' vs 'the body shape changed' are otherwise identical.
An eval set that lives on one machine is not an eval set.

decisions.decision: PR #22 merged by rebase, not squash
decisions.rationale: Squashing would collapse it back into the single 1181-line commit the local pre-commit gate rejected for mixed concerns.
Unchanged. The model contributed 0 of 7 published sentences; a hosted API would buy quality in the discarded step.

decisions.decision: A lane that cannot fail must not report a pass
decisions.rationale: tautological, no-ground, not-translated and no-tokens are four different ways of having nothing to say. --no-llm logged '0 findings, 42 tokens checked' where none of the 42 could have been missing.

decisions.decision: null and undefined do not collapse in an edition record
decisions.rationale: null is declared absence (backfilled edition, feeds gone); an absent key silently degraded the ground to the headline and produced a confident `fail` on a faithful summary.

decisions.decision: Edition 1 backfilled with sourceExcerpt: null rather than a reconstructed excerpt
decisions.rationale: Inventing one would produce a confident verdict about text the model never saw — the exact failure the file exists to avoid.

decisions.decision: An equivalence map must be bidirectional
decisions.rationale: ai->ia fixed the EN->PT lane and left PT->source false-positiving. A one-way fix reads as done and survived a whole session.

decisions.decision: Mutation harnesses test for green with a regex, never a fixed string
decisions.rationale: `grep -qF \"0 failed\"` matches \"10 failed\". Under-reporting is the bad direction: it sends you to add assertions that already exist.
It is the durable fix for the slot standoff but needs root and changes behaviour for every other ollama client on the machine. Named rather than decided by omission.

context_notes: Fourteen commits across five PRs (#22-#26), CI green on each, production smoked, and the Monday run rehearsed end to end with the model. Two through-lines. First: every gate shipped earlier in the session reported CLEAN somewhere it had no power to fail — a --no-llm run logged '0 findings, 42 tokens checked' where none of the 42 could have been missing. Second, and it kept recurring: a fix that addresses one direction reads as finished. The equivalence map fixed EN->PT and left PT->source broken; the ADR-001 comparison measured the LLM against the worst possible fallback; the mutation harness matched '10 failed' as '0 failed' and under-reported its own teeth. And three confident diagnoses of the Ollama hang were each wrong — stale runner, corrupt blob, embedding saturation — before the arithmetic showed 2.8 GB plus 595 MB on a 4 GB card. Everything here was found by running an instrument against real data or by mutating it. Nothing by re-reading it. Post-handoff, one more of the same family: a scan for leaked fixture servers matched ITSELF — `pgrep -f 'node -e'` hit the shell running the loop, because the loop's own text contained the pattern. A new PID appeared at every look and the kill took down my own command. Real leaked servers: zero. Scan by /proc/<pid>/comm, never by command text, and print the positive control beside the zero.
